purpose: Teach: 辻/ぃ/にゃ/かぁ/るる/之/燭/頁

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが街の辻に立つ地蔵にお参りされた
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he used to pray at that stone Jizo on the street corner.
lines.style: Soft, distant voice. Opening with gentle nostalgia. Slow, deliberate pacing—each image offered like a gift. Warm but touched by time. Trailing off slightly, as if seeing it again.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、子供達に「いいのかぃ?」って関西弁で聞かれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes—and he'd always scold you in that Kansai dialect, wouldn't he, dear? "Ii no kai?" "Is that alright?"
lines.style: Animated, warm recollection. A knowing laugh threaded through. Kansai inflection on the dialect. Affectionate teasing. Eyes crinkling at the memory of his strictness.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが猫を「にゃあ」と優しく呼ばれた
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, your father used to call to the cats so gently—"nyaa"—with such tenderness.
lines.style: Quieter now. The voice softens further. Almost a whisper on the cat's call. Reverent tone—speaking of gentleness as though it were sacred. Slow exhale at the end.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、「そっかぁ、それでええ」って関西弁で仰ってたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Oh yes—and he'd say in that Kansai way of his, "Sokka, sore de ee"—"I suppose that's fine." Just like him, wasn't it?
lines.style: Warm chuckle under the words. Kansai lilt natural and unselfconscious. Nodding rhythm to the speech. The affection of someone who knows exactly how he sounded. Gentle, familiar.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが「るるる」って小川の音を真似された
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, your father used to mimic the sound of the stream—"ruru ruru"—as if he were the water itself.
lines.style: Voice opens with childlike wonder. The mimicry is soft, onomatopoetic. Pause after the sound—letting it linger. Tone of marveling at a simple, perfect thing. Slightly breathless with the memory.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、「之」を含む古典をよく読まれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Mm—and when you were young, you read those classical texts with the character 之 in them all the time, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Observant, slightly playful. A gentle correction—drawing him into the shared past. Warm knowing. The pace is unhurried. Intimacy of someone who remembers what he studied.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは仏間の燭を毎晩灯された
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, your father lit the candles in the family altar every single night without fail.
lines.style: Reverent, almost ceremonial tone. Each word deliberate and weighted. Slow cadence—respecting the ritual being described. Quiet breath between phrases. A kind of sacred stillness in the voice.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、本を読まれる時、頁を丁寧にめくられたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes—and when you read your books, you turned every page so carefully, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Tender, intimate. Voice grows even softer, almost a whisper. The intimacy of two old people who know each other completely. A small, satisfied smile in the words. Warm close.
